description: Maps short-story (sub-story) message text IDs to the VoiceDataTable row used for the voice line played with each displayed message.

Id.simple: Message/text ID that keys the voice mapping.
Id.technical: FName native property and the export ImportKeyField; the JSON export spells the serialized property ID. Runtime does not call FindRow with this value on ShortStoryVoiceDataTable: GameScript_CollectRows flattens every typed row from DTM.ShortStoryVoiceDataTables (+0x780) in table order then row-name order, and ParseVoice takes the first row whose Id equals the current MessageId. AddLoadedDataTables receives only the ShortStoryVoiceDataTable loader, so this build has one source table; the supplied export has 580 unique keys and every key equals ID. MessageId is the sorted script-context message ID also passed to ParseMessage/ShowMessage, not the line/style/time FName arguments. For STDM_SS_ scripts GameScript_GetStoryTextId replaces STDM_SS_ with STDM_00 and appends 01 (STDM_SS_001 -> STDM_0000101), and GameTextManager finds all GameText IDs containing that key. All 580 exported voice-map IDs appear in all 11 ShortStoryDemoText locale exports (627 text IDs each); the other 47 text IDs have no row here. ParseVoice checks the DLC branch first, so a DLC-classified script uses DlcStoryDemoVoice tables even if its name contains STDM_SS_; only the non-DLC sub-story branch uses this table.

Id_Voice.simple: VoiceDataTable row to play for that message.
Id_Voice.technical: FName native property, exported as Id_Voice. In the non-DLC STDM_SS_ branch the first row matching Id passes this value to GameScript_FindVoiceRow over DTM.VoiceDataTables (+0x740), which uses FindRow<FGameDataTableRow_Voice> in table order and returns the first typed match; bCheckNone is false. Only VoiceDataTable is loaded into that array. ParseVoice copies the resolved Voice row's CueSheetName and CueName into a queued voice entry, with delay from the command's TimeId and Slot as the zero-based voice-player line index (0-3 in the ShowMessage variants). TEXT_TIME_NONE suppresses the entry; a numeric TimeId is its Atof value, a named TimeId uses ShowMessageTimeDataMap, and an absent name yields 0.0 (float seconds in the DeltaTime-based playback path). A missing mapping row or unresolved Voice row queues no voice; the Part cue sheet is still loaded by the separate hard-coded sub-story preload, so it is wrong to say Id_Voice supplies that preload. All 580 exported Id_Voice values resolve in the supplied VoiceDataTable export; each resolved row has CueSheetName Part and a CueName equal to its ID. The native default is NAME_None, but the export contains no empty values. PlayVoice later returns -1 for a disabled system-voice gate, an unloaded sheet, or no usable player slot.

notes: Loaded into DTM.ShortStoryVoiceDataTables (+0x780) from the single DataTable primary asset ShortStoryVoiceDataTable; AddLoadedDataTables filters null resolves, and this name has one loader (no shard array).

ParseVoice checks GameScript_IsDlcScript first (Script row + StoryDemo in-progress flag), so DLC scripts use DlcStoryDemoVoiceDataTable1/2 even if the name contains STDM_SS_. For other scripts, the STDM_SS_ substring selects this table; ordinary story demos use StoryDemoVoiceDataTable.

UGameScriptPlayer::UpdateLoad does not read this table or Id_Voice. For an STDM_SS_ script it directly adds cue sheet Part to the script load set; DLC and ordinary story scripts instead derive a sheet from the first matching row in their own voice-map tables, and gallery scripts use an empty hard-coded map.

Message IDs come from GameText IDs containing the derived script text ID. GameScript_GetStoryTextId maps STDM_SS_001 to STDM_0000101 by replacing STDM_SS_ with STDM_00 and appending 01; matching text IDs are sorted into the script context and advanced as ShowMessage commands run. The 580 mapped IDs are a subset of the 627 short-story text IDs in every supplied locale export; 47 have no voice mapping.

Lookup is deterministic first match: all typed rows are collected in DTM table order then row-name order, and FindByPredicate compares the native Id property. Only one ShortStoryVoiceDataTable asset and one VoiceDataTable asset are loaded in the reconstructed manager, so there is no observed cross-shard precedence here.

Export integrity: one asset, 580 rows, no empty keys or Id_Voice values, no key/ID mismatches, and every Id_Voice resolves in VoiceDataTable. Reused voice IDs are expected (for example VoPart_CP_030_22_00_010 appears on 13 message rows); all resolved cue sheets are Part in this export.

Failure/timing behavior is in ParseVoice and PlayVoice: TEXT_TIME_NONE skips voice queuing, missing mapping or Voice rows add no entry, delay is a float from the numeric/named TimeId (0.0 when unnamed and absent), Slot is the zero-based line index, and playback can still fail on a missing loaded sheet, disabled system voice, or unavailable player slot.

Behavioral statements are from reconstructed retail C++ with inline retail RVA annotations plus static exports. No retail Blueprint assets were available, so Blueprint-only references or overrides are not asserted; no editor launch, retail runtime test, network access, or retail-completeness claim was made.

usages.detail: Resolves the ShortStoryVoiceDataTable primary asset into DTM.ShortStoryVoiceDataTables (+0x780); this is the only loader passed to AddLoadedDataTables for that member.
GetRows collects every typed row table-by-table and row-name-by-row-name; ParseVoice then uses FindByPredicate on Id, making the first matching row win.
Derives the short-story GameText key from an STDM_SS_ script name (STDM_SS_001 -> STDM_0000101).
FindTextIdsContaining supplies the script message IDs whose containing text rows are sorted into the context consumed by ShowMessage and ParseVoice.
ParseVoice checks the DLC classification first; only the non-DLC else branch can choose the short-story table.
Detects STDM_SS_ in the script name to select the sub-story branch after the DLC check.
Collects all FGameDataTableRow_ShortStoryVoice rows from DTM.ShortStoryVoiceDataTables (+0x780).
Matches the current MessageId against each row's native Id property and takes the first hit.
Resolves the matched row's Id_Voice through GameScript_FindVoiceRow in DTM.VoiceDataTables (+0x740).
Copies the Voice row CueSheetName/CueName with GetMessageTime(TimeId) and the command Slot into the queued voice entry.
Sub-story script preload checks STDM_SS_ and hard-codes cue sheet Part instead of reading this table.
PlayVoice loads the queued cue sheet, selects or falls back to a voice-player slot, localizes the cue, and returns -1 on gate/sheet/slot failure.
Static export checked in full: one asset with 580 rows, key/ID equality, no empty Id_Voice, and all voice IDs reused across message rows.
